short: Sophocles was one of classical Athens' greatest tragic playwrights, celebrated for works like Oedipus Rex and Antigone.
full:
Born in 497 BCE, Sophocles dominated the dramatic competitions of the City Dionysia for decades, defeating older masters like Aeschylus. Over his long life, he wrote more than 120 plays, of which only seven have survived complete. He introduced significant innovations to Greek theatre, including the addition of a third actor, which allowed for more complex character interactions and reduced the narrative role of the chorus.

His plays are characterised by deep psychological insight, complex characters, and a focus on human agency struggling against fate and divine will. Masterpieces such as Oedipus Rex and Antigone remain foundational works of Western drama, continually performed and analysed for their timeless exploration of morality, duty, and tragedy.
